name: wasp-nest-envelope
title: Wasp Nest Envelope
description: A full-bleed paper/fibre backdrop modelled on paper-wasp nest construction: pulp is laid down in short fan-shaped mandible strokes that shingle into concentric layers around a hidden comb, each layer's tone a subtly different pulp batch, with a fixed cutaway wedge permanently exposing the banded interior and periodic wasp-visit stroke batches landing right at the growth front inside it.
instruction: Build <WaspNestEnvelope density? speed? paused? children? className? style?> as a full-bleed 2D-canvas paper/fibre pane growing wasp-nest envelope shells — layered pulp shingles, not a filled blob or a shader trick. REAL MECHANIC: paper wasps (Polistes, Vespula) scrape wood fibre, chew it into pulp, and lay it down in short fan-shaped mandible sweeps, each stroke slightly overlapping the last, building up in concentric shingled layers (like roof shingles or stucco passes) around the comb, with each layer's stroke direction and pulp-batch shade subtly different because different wasps forage different wood sources at different times (documented in Vespidae nest-architecture studies, e.g. Jeanne 1975 'The adaptiveness of social wasp nest architecture'). NUCLEATION: `round(min(w,h)/340)` independent points, minimum 1 (overridable via `density`), each growing its own shell from a fixed random (cx,cy). STROKE PRIMITIVE: a filled rect standing in for a short fan-shaped arc, length 14-22px (random per stroke), width 5-7px, positioned at angle = (strokeIndex * 11) / radius radians around the ring (STROKE_SPACING=11px along the circumference) and rotated tangent-to-ring plus a fan offset that cycles ((strokeIndex*14) % 42) - 21 degrees, giving the shingled fan-sweep look. STROKE RATE: 3.4 strokes/s per nest, landing one at a time (STROKE_INTERVAL_MS = 1000/3.4 ≈ 294ms) — this is the followable cadence. LAYER: a layer at radius r needs `ceil(2*PI*r/11)` strokes to complete; once filled, the shell radius steps +9px (LAYER_STEP) and a new layer starts, sampling a fixed toneOffset (-1..1) once. Growth stops adding new layers once the next radius would reach `1.15 * min(w,h)/2` (CAP) — at these rates that's ~40-70s for a typical hero, a slow background event, NOT the primary resting-loop signal. TONE: each stroke's fill is `mix(--ns-muted, --border, ageFraction)` (ageFraction = layer index / (layerCount-1), 0 = oldest/interior, 1 = newest/outermost) with the layer's fixed toneOffset applied as an RGB luminance multiplier `rgb * (1 + toneOffset * range)`, range = 0.08 in dark theme, 0.12 in light theme (`!documentElement.classList.contains('dark')`) where the token range compresses — NEVER a hue shift, NEVER touching --foreground or --ns-accent. RENDER SPLIT FOR PERFORMANCE AND LEGIBILITY: interior layers (all but the outermost 3) are drawn as a single solid stroked ring (`ctx.arc` + lineWidth = LAYER_STEP+1) in that layer's tone — this is what makes the concentric banding read clearly at card/hero distance without redrawing hundreds of stale strokes every frame. The outermost 3 layers (2 most-recently-completed plus the currently-active one) are drawn as INDIVIDUAL discrete strokes computed at that layer's angle formula, which is where the shingle-stroke texture is actually visible. CUTAWAY: each nest has a fixed 60-90deg wedge (`cutawayStart`, `cutawayWidth`, sampled once) permanently skipped when rendering strokes in the outermost-3 group ONLY — interior layers beneath render as full solid rings straight through that angular range, so the wedge exposes genuine banded cross-section, not a blank cut. Two thin `--border` radial lines are stroked at the wedge's two edges, from the radius where the outer group starts down to the current shell edge, reading as the cutaway's cut walls. WASP VISITS: every 5-8s (randomized per nest, re-rolled after each visit) a batch of 6-10 fresh strokes is generated at random angles INSIDE the cutaway's angular window, at the active layer's current radius, each with a 250ms alpha fade-in — since the cutaway is otherwise empty at the outer-group radii, these visit strokes are the only thing visible landing there, giving a fast, local, always-visible event riding on top of the much slower whole-shell growth. Visit strokes are pruned once shell growth buries them (`activeRadius - strokeRadius >= 22px`) or once a nest's list exceeds 60 entries (oldest dropped first) — this keeps memory bounded through the unbounded loop, including after a nest hits CAP and stops growing new layers (visits keep landing there forever, just recycling the same band). RESTING LOOP: t0 pre-seeds every nest 800-2200ms into its life (advanceNest run synchronously at mount) so a small stroke cluster and an already-thin exposed cutaway are visible immediately, never a blank canvas; by 2.5s several layers are stacked with visible banding and a visit batch may be mid-fade-in; by 5s the shell is visibly larger, more layers are banded, and the cutaway's exposed front has advanced — genuinely different geometry at each mark, driven by the always-running per-nest stroke accumulation even though full-shell closure (CAP) is a much longer background event. HOST: DPR-aware canvas (capped 2) sized off the host's own ResizeObserver-measured bounding box, never window size; nucleation points are re-seeded on resize only when the derived count itself changes, otherwise geometry persists. A single rAF loop (dt capped 48ms, scaled by `speed`) is stopped by an IntersectionObserver (threshold 0) when offscreen and by `visibilitychange` when the tab is hidden, restarted cleanly on return. `paused` freezes the clock without unmounting. REDUCED MOTION (SHELL_MIDGROWTH): matchMedia composes each nest directly (via the same `advanceNest` step function run synchronously, not the live rAF loop) to ~55% of its target radius — 5-6 banded layers, active layer's front fully laid so it reads mid-sweep, cutaway exposing clear internal banding — chosen because it is the one frame that legibly shows both the shingle-stroke texture and the layered banding at once (earlier shows no banding yet, later hides the cutaway's interior behind its own advancing front); a MutationObserver still repaints this frozen frame on a theme change. TOKENS: colours read only via `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` for `--background`, `--ns-muted`, `--border`, re-read on a MutationObserver watching documentElement's class, with no paint before that first read (checked on the rAF start, the ResizeObserver resume path, and the IntersectionObserver resume path). `--foreground` and `--ns-accent` never appear anywhere in the render — this stays a pure backdrop, never competing with overlaid headline copy. The canvas is aria-hidden/role=presentation; children render in an absolutely-positioned overlay above it and need a token scrim (bg-background/70 + backdrop-blur) since the layer bands span a wide value range in both themes.
useWhen: Pick wasp-nest-envelope when the backdrop should be an organic fibre/paper material building up in layered shingled bands with a structural cutaway exposing its cross-section — distinct from weld-pool (a molten-metal surface that carries a headline directly in its height field, not a background material) and from background-capillary-wick (ink wicking along a fixed fibre-vein lattice, a flow/absorption process rather than a growing layered shell). Pick brinicle-descent instead when the ambient process should be a vertical descend-and-release cycle rather than a radial layered buildup.
